result.name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A.
result.industry: Diversified retail and corporate banking (Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America)
markets: Retail and commercial banking in Mexico (BBVA México)
Banking in South America (Colombia, Peru, Argentina)
Digital banking in Italy and Germany

mission.statement: Support your drive to go further
mission.source: BBVA shareholders and investors website (Strategy 2025-2028, Purpose and Values) and 4Q25 corporate presentation
mission.plain: Help customers reach their goals by giving them the money tools and advice they need.

about.plain: BBVA is a big Spanish bank that keeps people's money safe and lends it out. It gives people bank accounts, cards, mortgages and car loans, and lends to companies big and small. Most of its money comes from Mexico and Spain, but it also runs banks in Turkey, Colombia, Peru and Argentina. Many customers use it almost entirely through its phone app.
about.customers: About 81 million active customers, from ordinary families and small shops to large companies and governments, mostly in Spain and Latin America.
about.everyday: If you pay with a BBVA card, use a BBVA cash machine in Spain or Mexico, or check your balance in its app, you are using BBVA.

money.plain: accounts, cards, consumer and business loans
accounts, mortgages, cards, business loans, funds
loans, cards and deposits in Turkey
banks in Colombia, Peru and Argentina

money.part: Rest of business (CIB in Europe, US and Asia; digital banks)
money.plain: lending and markets for big companies outside its home countries

money.part: Digital banks in Italy and Germany
money.plain: app-only accounts and savings for new European customers

result.summary: BBVA has a real but bank-sized advantage: it is a top-two lender in Mexico (26.17% of loans, May 2026), Turkey and Colombia, where scale, low-cost deposits and brand trust are hard to match, and it is known as one of the most digital big banks (62.6 million mobile customers, 66% of 2025's record 11.5 million new customers acquired digitally). That shows in a 38.8% cost-to-income ratio and 19.3% ROTE in 2025, but banking products are largely commodities, margins follow interest rates, and in Spain it is only the fourth bank by market share after its failed bid for Sabadell.

pricingPower.evidence: In H1 2026 net interest income rose 20.3% to EUR 15,164M and net fees 14.0% to EUR 4,572M while loans grew 17.7% at constant exchange rates, helped by high-margin lending in Mexico and Turkey; but in 2025 fees rose only 2.8% and NII 4.0% in euros, and lending margins follow central-bank rates and competition rather than BBVA's own pricing.

moats.evidence: BBVA is a trusted, century-old name and ranks #1 for NPS among large banks in Spain, Mexico and Peru (December 2025); Global Finance named it the World's Most Innovative Bank in 2026. Brand rarely lets a bank charge much more than rivals, though.
Payroll accounts, direct debits, mortgages and business credit lines make customers slow to move banks, though digital account opening and open banking have lowered the effort.
Its large client base in Mexico (number two bank) adds some payments and merchant density, but customers gain little directly from other customers banking with BBVA.

Scale and digital processes give it a 38.8% cost-to-income ratio in 2025 (target about 35%), well below most European peers, and low-cost deposits from 26.17% of Mexico's loan market and leading positions in Turkey and Colombia.
Banking licences, capital rules and branch/ATM networks limit entry; Mexico's banking market is concentrated among a few large banks, where BBVA ranks second (22.0% share in its 4Q25 presentation).
Its digital-only banks in Italy and Germany attack incumbents with lower-cost models, but they are small and fintechs such as Revolut and Nu do the same to BBVA.

Over a decade of digital transformation, a strong risk model in volatile emerging markets (Turkey, Argentina) and AI tools (eight AI initiatives and its 'The Frame' agent framework in 2026) are hard-won capabilities, though large rivals pursue the same.
BBVA has no exclusive licence or resource that rivals cannot obtain.

customers.evidence: At December 31, 2025 BBVA ranked #1 for net promoter score among large banks in Spain, Mexico and Peru, #2 in Turkey and Colombia and #3 in Argentina, and it added a record 11.5 million new customers in 2025 (81.2 million active clients).

talent.evidence: BBVA led the European financial sector in the Financial Times Europe's Best Employers 2026, was second in LinkedIn Top Companies Spain 2026, eighth in Time's World's Best Companies 2025, and is Merco Talento's best bank to work for in Spain.

product.evidence: Global Finance named BBVA the World's Most Innovative Bank and World's Best Bank in Emerging Markets (2026), and Euromoney named it the world's best bank for customer experience (2026 Awards for Excellence); 62.6 million customers use its mobile app.

threats: Heavy reliance on Mexico (about 40% of 2025 gross income and EUR 5,264M of EUR 10,511M net attributable profit) exposes it to Mexican rate cuts, peso weakness and politics.
Turkey and Argentina bring hyperinflation and currency risk; the weaker peso and lira cut 2025 euro profit growth to 4.5% versus 19.2% at constant exchange rates.
Falling interest rates in Europe and Mexico could compress net interest income, which was 71% of 2025 gross income.
Digital challengers such as Nu in Mexico and Colombia and Revolut in Europe target its most profitable retail customers.
In Spain it lacks the scale of CaixaBank and Santander after shareholders rejected its takeover of Banco Sabadell in October 2025 (only about 25% acceptance).
Spanish bank levies and tighter regulation, plus rising loan-loss provisions (impairments up 26.6% in H1 2026) as lending grows fast.

ceo.name: Onur Genç
ceo.background: Electrical and electronics engineer (Boğaziçi University), MBA Carnegie Mellon; McKinsey country manager in Istanbul (1999-2012), Garanti executive vice president (2012-2017), CEO of BBVA Compass in the US (2017)

c1.evidence: BBVA leads banking in Mexico (number two by share) and Colombia, but banking is a mature industry rather than an emerging, fast-growing one.

c2.evidence: Customers choose BBVA for its highly rated app and service (#1 NPS among large banks in Spain, Mexico and Peru in 2025) and its trusted brand, but digital features are copied by rivals within a few years.

c3.evidence: BBVA is a household name and recommended by customers in Spain and Mexico (#1 NPS among large banks in both), but it is not the default leader in global banking or in Spain, where it ranks fourth by market share.

c4.evidence: Its purpose 'Support your drive to go further' and sustainability financing goals are stressed in strategy materials, but management is chiefly judged on profit targets such as about EUR 48 billion of cumulative 2025-2028 profit.

c6.evidence: “big Spanish bank, digital, Mexico” are common first impressions; mostly positive among customers (#1 NPS among large banks in Spain and Mexico), though its hostile 2024-2025 bid for Sabadell drew political opposition in Spain.

c7.evidence: Its markets are large and growing in emerging economies (loans up 17.7% at constant FX in the 12 months to June 2026, Turkey 41.6% in local currency), with underbanked Mexico still a long runway, but banking does not ride a secular technology trend.

c8.evidence: It is expanding through digital-only banks in Italy and Germany and in corporate banking outside its home markets (Rest of Business loans up 52.5% at June 2026), though these are still about 5% of gross income.

m1.evidence: Onur Genç has pushed a clear digital and AI-led agenda (eight AI initiatives, 'The Frame' agent framework) and a goal of a cost-to-income ratio near 35%, but this is an evolution of an existing bank strategy rather than a radical vision.

m2.evidence: Genç is a professional executive (ex-McKinsey) who has been CEO since 2018, not a founder.

m4.evidence: BBVA ranks highly as an employer (top European financial firm in FT Europe's Best Employers 2026) and on customer NPS, but there is little specific public evidence of Genç's personal servant-leadership style.

m5.evidence: Under Genç BBVA was named Global Finance's World's Most Innovative Bank (2026) and keeps launching digital products, though the digital culture began under former chairman Francisco González and current chair Carlos Torres Vilá.

m6.evidence: Genç is trained as an electrical and electronics engineer (Boğaziçi University) and speaks often on digital and AI, but he is a banker and consultant rather than a hands-on technologist.

m7.evidence: There is no specific public evidence about Genç's personal causes beyond BBVA's sustainability and financial-inclusion programmes.

m7b.evidence: No commencement speech by Onur Genç at Stanford, Harvard, MIT or a similar top university was found; he has spoken in Carnegie Mellon's Tepper School speaker series.

m8b.evidence: Genç has a low-key, analytical public profile rather than a famous, distinctive personality.

m9.evidence: Since he became CEO, net attributable profit rose from EUR 1,305M (2020) to a record EUR 10,511M (2025) and the cost-to-income ratio fell to 38.8%, with H1 2026 profit up 11.1% to EUR 6,051M.

m10.evidence: BBVA runs one of the leanest big banks (38.8% cost-to-income in 2025) through digital processes, but it is not known for Bezos-style frugality.

c10.evidence: BBVA serves about 81 million active customers across Spain and Latin America and brings banking to many underbanked Mexicans, but its products are standard financial services offered by many banks.

p2.evidence: Running a safe, profitable bank across volatile economies such as Turkey and Argentina is difficult and important to those economies, but the products themselves are not technically unique.

f2.evidence: Profit before tax rose from 23.9% of gross income in 2020 (EUR 4,813M of 20,166M) to 43.9% in 2025 (EUR 16,227M of 36,931M), and cost-to-income improved from 45.1% to 38.8%; banks report no gross margin.

f3.evidence: Shareholders' equity is positive and the CET1 capital ratio was 12.90% at June 30, 2026, above its 11.5-12% target, but like every bank it funds itself mostly with deposits and debt.

f4.evidence: Operating income (before provisions) rose every year from EUR 11,079M (2020) to EUR 22,599M (2025); operating cash flow at a bank swings with deposits and lending, so it is not a meaningful trend.

v1.evidence: BBVA's app and service rank first for NPS among large banks in Spain, Mexico and Peru, a practical reason to choose it, but rivals such as CaixaBank, Santander and Nu offer similar products.

v2.evidence: BBVA led the European financial sector in FT Europe's Best Employers 2026, ranked second in LinkedIn Top Companies Spain 2026, eighth in Time's World's Best Companies 2025 and is Merco Talento's best bank to work for in Spain.

c5.evidence: Tens of millions of customers in Mexico, Spain, Turkey and South America would lose accounts, cards and loans overnight, and BBVA México is systemic to Mexico's economy, but other banks would eventually replace it.
